chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by a clean twelve-fold enumeration of cosmic judges — a systematic substrate teaching with strong structural integrity. Each judge is mapped to a cosmic being and a judicial function; both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system. The enumeration is bookended by an introduction (¶2) and a recapitulation (¶15) that form an inclusio around the Father of Greatness. Only ¶1 (dialogue frame) and ¶16 (exhortation) are clearly later layers, plus one institutional insertion ('holy church') in ¶13. The editorial fatigue data confirms the exhortation shift in the final paragraph. The ¶15 seam flag is a false positive — it is a recapitulation with 0.0 institutional vocabulary, not an institutional extension. The teaching purity (0.729) reflects the dominant substrate layer with minimal overlay.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure formulaic dialogue frame: 'Once again he speaks to his disciples.' No cosmological content. Bridge connective flag correctly identifies this as frame.

paragraphs.core_text: Twelve judges exist; the great mighty givers of judgement! They were sent and came from the exalted greatness to this place. They were assigned to different works according to the command that the Judge, who belongs to the greatness, entrusted to all these judges. Now he, the great Judge, he who transcends all the judges, who exists and is established in the aeons of greatness; he is the Father of Greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Establishes the cosmological framework: twelve judges emanated from the Father of Greatness as transcendent Judge. Systematic, impersonal, structural. Both sides of the mapping (judges ← greatness) stay within the cosmic system. This paragraph sets up the enumeration structure that ¶3-14 will fill.

paragraphs.core_text: The first judge is the First Man, he who humiliated the ruler of Darkness in the beginning. He judged him according to a judgement of righteousness; for he had exalted himself against a kingdom that was not his own.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumeration unit #1. First Man → cosmic judicial function against the ruler of Darkness. Both sides within the cosmic system. 'In the beginning' anchors to cosmic time, not historical time.

paragraphs.core_text: The second judge is the Living Spirit, he who came and bore up the Man. He too made a judgement on all the powers of Darkness; which had wounded the garments of the First Man.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumeration unit #2. Living Spirit → rescue of First Man and judgement on powers of Darkness. 'Garments of the First Man' is cosmic-correspondential vocabulary (garments = the five light elements). Pure substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: The third judge is the Mother of Life, the Great Spirit, she who beautified and set up the heavenly part of the universe, according to her pleasure; which [...] her. She judged the rulers above; she fettered and set them firmly in the place that is fitting for them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumeration unit #3. Mother of Life → cosmic architectural function and judgement of the rulers. Lacuna present. Both sides within cosmic system. 'Fettered and set them firmly' describes cosmic binding.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth judge is the Great Builder, he who built the new aeon of joy. He judged, according to a judgement of righteousness, the storehouses of the enemy; that death may not well up from this time on. He has constructed a prison for the enemy. Also, upon the crown of the building he has constructed a throne for the First Man and all the fathers of light; they who engaged the struggle with the evil one and were victorious over him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumeration unit #4. Great Builder → cosmic construction (new aeon, prison, throne). All cosmic architecture. 'Storehouses of the enemy' is systematic cosmic vocabulary. Longest enumeration unit — the Builder's dual function (prison for enemy, throne for light) is elaborated.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.80⟩
The fifth judge is the great King of Honour, he who dwells and is established in the seventh firmament. He is the judge of all the firmaments who gives a true judgement, according to a judgement of righteousness, upon all the powers and all the kingdoms of the firmaments.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumeration unit #5. King of Honour → seventh firmament → judge of all firmaments. Cosmic geography (seventh firmament, kingdoms of the firmaments). Both sides within cosmic system. The King of Honour will recur in the recapitulation (¶15).

paragraphs.core_text: The sixth judge is [the Th]ird Ambassador, he who came and displayed his image. He purified the light [...] which his own [...] also of the enemy, he has [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumeration unit #6. Third Ambassador → image display and light purification. Heavily damaged by lacunae. What remains is cosmic — 'displayed his image' and 'purified the light' are cosmic process descriptions.

paragraphs.core_text: The seventh judge is ... ... the worlds [... as he gives the victory to] they who are steadfast; but he condemns the ones who are convicted ... ... he shall become for them the steps of the way (?) [...]; but the convicted he sweeps and casts out to the depths.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumeration unit #7. Very heavily damaged. The name of the seventh judge is lost. What survives describes cosmic judicial separation (victory to steadfast, casting convicted to depths). 'The depths' is cosmic geography.

paragraphs.core_text: The eighth judge is Jesus the Splendour, the father of all the apostles; because after the Ambassador had displayed his image and the light was taken [...] a mass of rulers rose up from above and below. Then they sent Jesus the Splendour. He came ... ... he descended and made a judgement in the firmaments. He separated the steadfast from the convicted.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumeration unit #8. Jesus the Splendour is a cosmic entity in the Manichaean emanation hierarchy, not the historical Jesus. 'The father of all the apostles' is borderline — it could be an editorial epithet linking to apostolic succession, or it could describe Jesus the Splendour's cosmic function as source of the apostolic manifestation (he sends the Light Mind). I retain it as substrate because the phrase describes a cosmic role, but flag the ambiguity. The rest is clearly cosmic process: rulers rising, descent, judgement in firmaments.

paragraphs.core_text: The ninth judge is the Virgin of Light, [she who took the heart] of the powers by her image, gathering her own ones into her. She makes a judgement on the ruler of the moist, and the ruler of the dry.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumeration unit #9. Virgin of Light → image-seduction of powers → judgement on cosmic rulers. 'The ruler of the moist, and the ruler of the dry' are cosmic correspondences mapping elemental domains to archontic rulers. Pure substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: The tenth judge is the Judge who dwells in the atmosphere, judging all mankind. He makes a separation between they who are good and they who are evil, setting apart the righteous from the sinners.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumeration unit #10. The cosmic Judge in the atmosphere — cosmic geography. His function is cosmic-judicial separation. 'All mankind' and 'righteous from sinners' could edge toward application, but they describe the cosmic function of this judge within the system, not a specific contemporary situation. The 'atmosphere' as cosmic zone keeps both sides within the system.

paragraphs.core_text: The eleventh judge is the Light Mind, he who shall come and appear in the world. And he unveils [...] and separates light from darkness, and sets the truth apart from lawlessness.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'and he chooses the holy church' — 'holy church' (ⲧⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲁⲃ) reaches outside the cosmic system to identify the institutional Manichaean community. The mapping crosses from cosmos→institution. This is confirmed by the institutional vocabulary score of 12.82.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumeration unit #11. The Light Mind's cosmic functions (appearing in the world, separating light from darkness, setting truth apart from lawlessness) are substrate. 'He chooses the holy church' is an editorial insertion that maps the Light Mind's function onto the institutional community — one side of the mapping leaves the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: The twelfth judge is the great counsel, which is the summons and the obedience, which is appointed in the elements. It is the one that makes a separation between the good and the evil ones. At the end also it can gather itself together and sculpt its own self in the Last Statue. And it separates light from darkness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumeration unit #12. 'The great counsel' = cosmic entity. 'Summons and obedience' = the Call and the Answer, a fundamental cosmic pair. 'Appointed in the elements' = cosmic placement. 'Last Statue' = the cosmic eschatological concept of the final gathering of all light. All within the cosmic system. This closes the twelve-fold enumeration.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the twelve great and mighty judges who were sent. They came from the great Judge, he who transcends all the judges. He is the Father that is hidden and immeasurable, the one who exists; who is established in the aeons of greatness upon the great throne of honour, which is the King of Honour [...] in his kingdom.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The seam flag here is a false positive. This is a recapitulation that forms an inclusio with ¶2, returning to the Father of Greatness as transcendent Judge. Institutional vocabulary score is 0.0. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system (aeons of greatness, throne of honour, King of Honour, kingdom). 'These are the twelve' is a natural closing formula for enumeration teaching, not an editorial bridge connective. The substrate score (18.33) is the highest in the chapter.

Clear exhortation/devotional closure. Every diagnostic marker fires: first-person address ('I am telling you about this, my beloved ones'), moral imperative ('walk in true heart on this path of righteousness'), community instruction ('May a brother speak with his brother in truth'), eschatological promise ('receive the victory from these twelve great judges, and go to rest in this place of rest for ever'). The exhortation score (25.0) is the highest in the chapter. Editorial fatigue confirmed: this is appended after the complete substrate teaching (¶2-15).
